content: Dental instruments are specialized tools utilized by dental professionals to perform various dental treatments. These instruments are designed for examining, manipulating, restoring, and removing teeth, as well as addressing surrounding oral structures. Standard Instruments Standard dental instruments are employed for examining, restoring, extracting teeth, and manipulating oral tissues. Examination Instruments These tools are essential for manipulating oral tissues to enhance visual access during dental examinations or treatments. Dental Mirror Dental mirrors are used by dentists or dental auxiliaries to view a reflected image of teeth in areas of the mouth where direct visibility is challenging or impossible. They are also employed to reflect light onto specific surfaces and to retract soft tissues, improving access and visibility. Tweezers Tweezers are used for handling small objects or materials during dental procedures. Probes Sickle Probe (Dental Explorer): Used to detect cavities, calculus, or other irregularities on the tooth surface. Periodontal Probe: Measures pocket depths around teeth to assess periodontal health. Straight Probe: Used for general examination and detection of caries. Retractors Retractors are tools used to hold back soft tissues, such as cheeks, lips, or the tongue, to improve access and visibility during procedures. Examples include: Mouth prop Dental mirror Cheek retractor Tongue retractor Lip retractor Local Anesthesia Dental anesthesia is administered using dental syringes to numb specific areas of the mouth during procedures. Dental Drills Dental drills are categorized based on their speed and function: High-speed air-driven drills: Used for cutting hard tissues like enamel and dentin. Slow-speed drills: Used for polishing or removing soft carious material. Friction grip drills: Designed for high-speed handpieces. Surgical handpieces: Used in oral surgery. Straight handpieces with Christmas tree burs: Utilized for specific cutting tasks. Burs Dental burs are cutting tools made from materials such as multi-fluted tungsten carbide, diamond-coated tips, or stainless steel. They come in various shapes and sizes, classified by their shank type and intended use: Round burs (sizes ¼ to 10): Commonly used for cavity preparation. Inverted cone burs (sizes 33½ to 37L): Used for creating undercuts. Latch-type burs: Used in slow-speed handpieces with contra-angle attachments. Friction grip burs: Small burs used exclusively in high-speed handpieces. Operative Burs Operative burs are available in various shapes, including flat fissure, pear-shaped, football, round, tapered, flame, chamfer, bevel, and bud burs. They may also include specialized types like steel inverted cone burs, diamond burs, and polishing stones (e.g., brown stone, green stone). Restorative Instruments Restorative instruments are used for repairing and restoring teeth. Excavators Spoon Excavator: Removes soft carious decay. Half Hollenbach: Tests for overhangs or flash in restorations. Chisels: Used for beveling the cavosurface margin in cavity preparations. Examples include: Straight Chisel: Used in Class 3, 4, and 5 cavity preparations on the maxillary teeth. Wedelstaedt Chisel: Used in anterior teeth for Class 3, 4, and 5 cavities. Bin Angle Chisel: Held in a pen grasp and used for Class 2 maxillary cavities. Burnishers Burnishers are used to smooth and polish restorations. Examples include: Flat plastic burnisher Ball burnisher Beaver tail burnisher Cone burnisher Pluggers Pluggers are used to condense restorative materials into cavity preparations. Examples include: Amalgam plugger 49 plugger Periodontal Scalers Periodontal scalers are used for removing calculus and plaque from tooth surfaces. Curettes Universal Curettes: Designed for use on all tooth surfaces. Gracey Curettes: Designed for specific tooth surfaces and areas. Ultrasonic Scalers Ultrasonic scalers use high-frequency vibrations to remove calculus and plaque efficiently. Prosthodontic Instruments Prosthodontic instruments are used in the fabrication and adjustment of dental prostheses. Removable Prosthodontics Examples include: Spatula Fox plane Willis gauge Bunsen burner Wax knife Le Cron carver Calipers Extraction and Surgical Instruments Extraction and surgical instruments are used for tooth removal and oral surgery. Dental Forceps Dental forceps are designed for extracting teeth and come in various types, such as: Upper Universals Upper Universal Fine Lower Universals Upper Canine Upper Straight Long Upper Straight Short Upper Right Molar Upper Left Molar Upper Wisdom Tooth Greyhound Root forceps Bayonet forceps Elevators Elevators are used to loosen teeth or roots before extraction. Examples include: Narrow and wide straight elevators Curved luxators Coupland’s elevators Warwick James elevators Cryer elevators Periosteal elevators Root-tip picks Potts elevators Cogswell-A elevators Chisels Chisels, such as osteotomes, are used for cutting or reshaping bone during surgical procedures. Orthodontic Instruments Orthodontic instruments are used for adjusting and placing orthodontic appliances. Examples include: Ligature cutters Distal end cutters Weingart pliers Endodontic Instruments Endodontic instruments are used in root canal therapy. Examples include: K-files Hedstrom files Gates Glidden drills Finger spreaders Lentulo spirals Straight probes Apex locators Microscopes Pluggers
